arxiv-2005-03353.title: Distributional robustness of K-class estimators and the PULSE Published in The Econometrics Journal: https://doi.org/10.1093/ectj/utab031
arxiv-2005-03353.creator: Martin Emil Jakobsen, Jonas Peters
arxiv-2005-03353.description: Abstract While causal models are robust in that they are prediction optimal under arbitrarily strong interventions, they may not be optimal when the interventions are bounded. We prove that the classical K-class estimator satisfies such optimality by establishing a connection between K-class estimators and anchor regression.

arxiv-2309-11829.title: Making Mathematical Research Data FAIR: A Technology Overview
arxiv-2309-11829.creator: Tim Conrad, Eloi Ferrer, Daniel Mietchen, Larissa Pusch, Johannes Stegmüller, Moritz Schubotz
arxiv-2309-11829.description: Abstract The sharing and citation of research data is becoming increasingly recognized as an essential building block in scientific research across various fields and disciplines. Sharing research data allows other researchers to reproduce results, replicate findings, and build on them. Ultimately, this will foster faster cycles in knowledge generation.

arxiv-2311-15541.title: Neural Network Applications to Improve Drift Chamber Track Position Measurements
arxiv-2311-15541.creator: D. Palo, W. Molzon
arxiv-2311-15541.description: Abstract This paper describes applications of two neural networks to improve drift chamber position measurements. One network calculates a data-driven estimate of the drift cell time-to-distance relationship that is conventionally estimated by a numerical calculation based on the anode and cathode wire geometry, wire potentials, and gas properties.

arxiv-2403-07236.title: Partial Identification of Individual-Level Parameters Using Aggregate Data in a Nonparametric Model Thanks: I am especially grateful to Edward Vytlacil, Isaiah Andrews, and Anna Mikusheva for their guidance and advice. I thank Alberto Abadie, Hyungsik Roger Moon, Whitney Newey, Jesse Shapiro, Elie T
arxiv-2403-07236.creator: Sarah Moon
arxiv-2403-07236.description: Abstract I develop a methodology to partially identify linear combinations of conditional mean outcomes when the researcher only has access to aggregate data. Unlike the existing literature, I only allow for marginal, not joint, distributions of covariates in my model of aggregate data.

arxiv-2405-17554.title: Stepping into the Forest: Confronting Interacting Radiation Models for the Hubble Tension with Lyman- α \alpha Data
arxiv-2405-17554.creator: Hengameh Bagherian, Melissa Joseph, Martin Schmaltz, Eashwar N. Sivarajan
arxiv-2405-17554.description: Abstract Models of interacting dark radiation have been shown to alleviate the Hubble tension. Extensions incorporating a coupling between dark matter and dark radiation (DM-DR) have been proposed as combined solutions to both the Hubble and S 8 S_{8} tensions.

arxiv-2408-09189.title: SA-GDA: Spectral Augmentation for Graph Domain Adaptation
arxiv-2408-09189.creator: Jinhui Pang, Zixuan Wang, Jiliang Tang, Mingyan Xiao, Nan Yin
arxiv-2408-09189.description: Abstract . Graph neural networks (GNNs) have achieved impressive impressions for graph-related tasks. However, most GNNs are primarily studied under the cases of signal domain with supervised training, which requires abundant task-specific labels and is difficult to transfer to other domains. There are few works focused on domain adaptation for graph node classification.

arxiv-2411-10185.title: Efficient Progressive Image Compression with Variance-aware Masking
arxiv-2411-10185.creator: Alberto Presta 1 Enzo Tartaglione 2 Attilio Fiandrotti 1,2 Marco Grangetto 1 Pamela Cosman 3 1 University of Turin, Italy 2 LTCI, Télécom Paris, Institut Polytechnique de Paris 3 Dept. of Electrical and Computer Engineering, UC San Diego, CA, USA alberto.presta@unito.it
arxiv-2411-10185.description: Abstract Learned progressive image compression is gaining momentum as it allows improved image reconstruction as more bits are decoded at the receiver. We propose a progressive image compression method in which an image is first represented as a pair of base-quality and top-quality latent representations.

arxiv-2502-19781.title: RANGE: Retrieval Augmented Neural Fields for Multi-Resolution Geo-Embeddings
arxiv-2502-19781.creator: Aayush Dhakal Srikumar Sastry Subash Khanal Adeel Ahmad Eric Xing Nathan Jacobs, Washington University in St. Louis, Taylor Geospatial Institute
arxiv-2502-19781.description: Abstract The choice of representation for geographic location significantly impacts the accuracy of models for a broad range of geospatial tasks, including fine-grained species classification, population density estimation, and biome classification. Recent works like SatCLIP and GeoCLIP learn such representations by contrastively aligning geolocation with co-located images.

arxiv-2507-00386.title: Complete Boundary Phase Diagram of the Spin- 1 2 \frac{1}{2} XXZ Chain with Boundary Fields in the Anti-Ferromagnetic Gapped Regime
arxiv-2507-00386.creator: Parameshwar R. Pasnoori, Yicheng Tang, Junhyun Lee, J. H. Pixley, Patrick Azaria, Natan Andrei
arxiv-2507-00386.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Parameshwar R. Pasnoori, Yicheng Tang, Junhyun Lee, J. H. Pixley, Patrick Azaria, Natan Andrei. We consider the spin 1 2 \frac{1}{2} XXZ chain with diagonal boundary fields and solve it exactly using Bethe ansatz in the gapped anti-ferromagnetic regime and obtain the complete phase boundary diagram.

arxiv-2507-13427.title: Two-photon coupling via Josephson element II: Interaction renormalizations and cross-Kerr coupling
arxiv-2507-13427.creator: E. V. Stolyarov, V. L. Andriichuk, A. M. Sokolov
arxiv-2507-13427.description: Abstract We study the interactions mediated by symmetric superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID), their renormalizations, and applicability of the anharmonic oscillator model for a coupled phase qubit. The coupling SQUID can switch between single- or two-photon interaction in situ . We consider a coupled resonator and an rf SQUID.

arxiv-2512-00656.title: Sycophancy Claims about Language Models: The Missing Human-in-the-Loop
arxiv-2512-00656.creator: Jan Batzner, Volker Stocker, Stefan Schmid, Gjergji Kasneci
arxiv-2512-00656.description: Abstract Sycophantic response patterns in Large Language Models (LLMs) have been increasingly claimed in the literature. We review methodological challenges in measuring LLM sycophancy and identify five core operationalizations. Despite sycophancy being inherently human-centric, current research does not evaluate human perception.

gao-gaoreports-gao-06-230.description: Federal Compensation Programs: Perspectives on Four Programs (2005).

pmc-12593846.title: Association between cumulative blood pressure and the risk of cognitive impairment in Chinese older adults: a longitudinal study over 16 years
pmc-12593846.creator: Ying Gao, Peng Zhang, Hongxi Yang, Shu Li, Haiyan Su, Qing Zhang
pmc-12593846.description: BackgroundCumulative blood pressure (BP), which takes into account both the magnitude and duration of BP exposure, is linked to cognitive impairment. However, this association remains unclear in Chinese older adults. The critical level of cumulative BP associated with significantly increased cognitive impairment risk remains elusive.

pmc-12665244.title: Recent Advances in Understanding the Clinical Implications of Heterogeneous Drug Resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae
pmc-12665244.creator: Jianhua Fang, Hongyi Lai, Huade Chen, Zhibo Tao, Na Cheng, Tianxin Xiang
pmc-12665244.description: Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP), a clinically significant Gram-negative opportunistic pathogen, has emerged as one of the predominant causative agents of hospital-acquired infections (HAIs). This bacterium is responsible for various severe clinical manifestations, including pneumonia, urinary tract infections, bloodstream infections, and sepsis. In recent years, the global prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) K. pneumoniae strains has been escalating rapidly.

pmc-13422804.title: Regional differences and influencing factors of needlestick injury protection among clinical nurses in China: a national cross-sectional survey based on economic region
pmc-13422804.creator: Ying Shen, Guangwei Liu, Liping Liu, Yan Yin, Hongtao Tie, Yue Shao, Lu Liu, Kexue Pu, Haiyan Yao, Xiaoping Jiang, Liping Wu, Xiaoping Luo, Wenfeng Tang, Rui He

pmc-13587914.title: Cardiovascular risk estimation using the steno type 1 risk engine in Brazilian individuals with type 1 diabetes: a multicenter cross-sectional study
pmc-13587914.creator: Marília Brito Gomes, Fernanda Oliveira Braga de Albuquerque, Alessandra Matheus, Luiz Henrique Canani, Adriana Costa Forti, Reine Marie Chaves, Elizabeth João Pavin, Renan Montenegro Junior, Sergio A Dib, João S Felicio, Rosangela Roginski Réa, Marcia Nery, Carlos Antonio Negrato, Luana Casari Silva
pmc-13587914.description: Highlights•Individuals with type 1 diabetes face high cardiovascular risk and mortality.•Steno type 1 risk engine helps identify cardiovascular risk in type 1 diabetes.•Retinopathy, late diagnosis, hs-CRP, and uric acid can be correlated to high cardiovascular risk.•Cardioprotective drugs are underused in moderate and high-risk Brazilian individuals with T1D.•Identifying risk factors may improve prevention of cardiovascular disease in individuals with T1D.

pmc-13595276.title: Hepatic translational rewiring in insulin deficiency identifies Reg3α as an insulin-independent glucoregulatory factor
pmc-13595276.creator: Pryscila D S Teixeira, Sarah Mathilda Vincent, Romane Meurs, Gloria Ursino, Szabolcs Zahoran, Giulia Lucibello, Marcella M Authiat, Anne-Claude Gavin, Giorgio Ramadori, Roberto Coppari
pmc-13595276.description: ContextInsulin deficiency (ID) causes severe metabolic defects and death if untreated, while insulin therapy does not fully restore metabolic homeostasis. Leptin therapy corrects metabolic abnormalities and promotes survival in rodents unable to produce insulin, suggesting the existence of insulin-independent glucoregulatory mechanisms.ObjectiveTo characterize hepatic translational remodeling in severe insulin deficiency and determine whether leptin-responsive translational changes can reveal novel glucoregulatory factors.

pmc-13633404.title: Iliofemoral Deep Vein Thrombosis Despite Repeatedly Negative D‐Dimer Results
pmc-13633404.creator: Rova Malala Fandresena Randrianarisoa, Mounia Harici Stamboul, Yassine Haoues, Gerda Menzato, Amirouche Bessaoudi, Mostefa Koroghli, Catherine Letrillard
pmc-13633404.description: A 75‐year‐old man presented with a three‐week history of left lower‐limb pain and repeatedly negative D‐dimer results. Doppler ultrasonography ultimately revealed extensive iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis (DVT). This case highlights that a negative D‐dimer result does not exclude subacute DVT and that clinical suspicion should prevail over biomarker findings.

pmc-13634522.title: Literacy-sensitive sexual and reproductive health education for adolescents in Ghana: Evidence from a school-based quasi-experimental study
pmc-13634522.creator: Jacqueline Nkrumah
pmc-13634522.description: ObjectivesThis study examined how the complexity and format of sexual and reproductive health (SRH) education materials influence adolescents’ functional SRH literacy and its implications for literacy-sensitive SRH education.Study designQuasi-experimental study design.MethodsThis school-based quasi-experimental study was conducted among 317 adolescents aged 11–15 years (grades 7–8) in the Effutu Municipality.

uslaw-usc-t42-s2000aa11.title: 42 U.S.C. § 2000aa–11 — Guidelines for Federal officers and employees
uslaw-usc-t42-s2000aa11.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s2000aa11.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 21A (Privacy Protection); Subchapter II (Attorney General Guidelines). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Procedures to obtain documentary evidence; protection of certain privacy interests The Attorney General shall, within six months of October 13, 1980, issue guidelines for the procedures to be employed by any Federal officer or employee, in connection.
